feed.title: WatchmanHQ: patch now
feed.subtitle: Flaws attackers are exploiting (CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog) in equipment small firms run, named in recent threat reports.
feed.rights: Published by WatchmanHQ (https://watchmanhq.com). Free, best effort, provided as is, with no warranty of any kind. Check the vendor's advisory before you change a device. CISA's catalog is public domain (CC0); these alerts are CC BY 4.0: credit WatchmanHQ.

entry.title: Exploited again: ConnectWise ScreenConnect (CVE-2024-1708)
entry.summary: Remote support or IT management (ConnectWise). ConnectWise ScreenConnect Path Traversal Vulnerability. ConnectWise ScreenConnect contains a path traversal vulnerability which could allow an attacker to execute remote code or directly impact confidential data and critical systems. CISA listed it as exploited on 2026-04-28, and it is used in ransomware attacks. Install the vendor's update, or its workaround until there is one, then follow the advisory's steps to look for signs of compromise: an update closes the hole, it does not remove an attacker who got in first. If the device gets no more updates (past its end of life), take it off the internet and replace it. Reported by: Huntress, 2026-10-20; Huntress, 2026-10-12.

entry.title: Exploited again: Synacor Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) (CVE-2025-27915)
entry.summary: Email server (Zimbra). Synacor Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) Cross-site Scripting Vulnerability. Synacor Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that exists in the Classic Web Client due to insufficient sanitization of HTML content in ICS files. When a user views an e-mail message containing a malicious ICS entry, its embedded JavaScript executes via an ontoggle event inside a tag. This allows an attacker to run arbitrary JavaScript within the victim's session, potentially leading to unauthorized actions such as setting e-mail filters to redirect messages to an attacker-controlled address. As a result, an attacker can perform unauthorized actions on the victim's account, including e-mail redirection and data exfiltration. CISA listed it as exploited on 2025-10-07. Install the vendor's update, or its workaround until there is one, then follow the advisory's steps to look for signs of compromise: an update closes the hole, it does not remove an attacker who got in first.
